current_activity: directing defence of Normandy from Le Mans HQ
notes: Seventh Army HQ at Le Mans (Dollmann) on D-Day; initially did most of the fighting; XXV Corps (Brittany) per CMH.

commander: Generaloberst Friedrich Dollmann (died 28 June); SS-Obergruppenführer Paul Hausser appointed at 15:00
notes: Dollmann died (heart attack) 28 June per CMH and Wikipedia Operation Epsom (Wikipedia's Dollmann page says 29 June; conflict G001). Hausser (II SS Pz Corps) appointed 7th Army commander at 15:00, Bittrich took II SS Pz Corps; at 17:00 7th Army to face the American front, Panzer Group West the Anglo-Canadian front.

commander: Generaloberst Friedrich Dollmann (died 29 June per this claim)
location_qualifier: 7th Army HQ; Dollmann died there per Wikipedia
notes: Wikipedia's Friedrich Dollmann page gives his death as 29 June 1944 at Le Mans, one day later than CMH / Operation Epsom (28 June). Competing claim to the preferred row.

current_activity: army command post at Le Mans; Kluge for the second day commanding the army and the LXXXIV Corps himself
notes: Event date: on the morning of 31 July Kluge, at the Seventh Army command post in Le Mans, was for the second day 'for all intents and purposes commanding the LXXXIV Corps and the Seventh Army' besides his duties as OB West and Army Group B commander (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 17 p. 323). Commander: Hausser remained the army commander (ch. 17 p. 328); the row names him and records Kluge's direct control here.

current_activity: army attack from the Mortain area toward Avranches (Operation Luttich) with the XLVII Panzer Corps
notes: Event date: the attack started shortly after midnight on 6/7 August, without artillery preparation; Hausser had only delayed the jump-off to midnight to give the 1st SS Panzer Division two hours more (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 24 p. 462-463). Location approximate: the source names the attack zone around Mortain, not an army headquarters site (administrative personnel had been evacuated from Le Mans, long the Seventh Army headquarters, after the loss of Laval; ch. 22 p. 435); the point is Mortain (10 km). Opponents: the US 30th Division (ch. 24 p. 462-463).

commander: SS-Oberst-Gruppenfuehrer Paul Hausser (seriously wounded; successor Funck or Eberbach, see notes)
current_activity: army commander Hausser seriously wounded in the Falaise pocket; successor named differently by the sources
notes: Event date: Hausser, the Seventh Army commander, was brought out of the pocket seriously wounded on 20 August (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 27 p. 553, 557). Review (open point; commander not stated consistently): ch. 27 p. 557 says that Funck, the XLVII Panzer Corps commander, took temporary command of the Seventh Army; ch. 31 p. 663 says the army was commanded by Eberbach after Hausser was wounded; Wikipedia's Eberbach page gives him as commander of the Seventh Army from 21 to 30 August. The row records Hausser as the commander on the date and the successor as unresolved. Location approximate: the army headquarters stood inside the pocket (ch. 27 p. 537); the point is the pocket area (10 km).

commander: SS-Oberst-Gruppenfuehrer Paul Hausser (seriously wounded; successor Funck or Eberbach, see the command-change row)
current_activity: Model subordinates the Seventh Army to the Fifth Panzer Army (Dietrich)
notes: Event date: Model on 20 August subordinated the Seventh Army to the Fifth Panzer Army, perhaps because Hausser had been wounded and evacuated, giving Dietrich command of the whole area from the coast to the First Army boundary (Breakout and Pursuit ch. 28 p. 576; ch. 27 p. 557). Relationship: the source says 'subordinated'; it does not say assigned or attached, so the relation is unspecified_subordination. Location approximate: the point is the pocket area (10 km), as for the command-change row of the same day.

location_qualifier: line to be held, not the army headquarters
current_activity: The Führer orders the Seventh Army to hold the Meuse and the canal west of Maastricht as long as possible
notes: Event date: Schramm, OKW war diary, p. 370, entry of 9 September: the Führer ordered "daß die 7. Armee weiter hinhaltend vor dem Westwall kämpfen und" "die Maas und den Kanal westlich Maastricht halten solle". Event definition: the order of 9 September (early morning); it is an order, not a report of the line held. Event support: one OKW war diary entry. Location: Maastricht, named in the order as the end of the line to be held, with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: the objective line is a town point. Location support: the war diary names Maastricht. Commander: General der Panzertruppen Erich Brandenberger. Context: the same entry has the I SS Panzer Corps keep contact with the XLVII Panzer Corps on its right.

location_qualifier: army right wing at Aachen; the army headquarters place is not stated
current_activity: OB West names the right wing of the Seventh Army at Aachen the main danger point and orders Aachen held to the last
notes: Event date: Schramm, OKW war diary, p. 404, entry of 9 October: OB West judged "der Hauptgefahrenpunkt" of the whole western front to lie on "dem rechten Flügel der 7. Armee"; "Aachen bis zum letzten zu verteidigen" ... "befohlen worden". Event definition: the assessment of 9 October; the same entry accepts the possible loss of the 246th Infantry Division. Event support: one OKW war diary entry. Location: Aachen with a precision of 25 km. Location approximate: a sector point for the army right wing. Location support: the war diary names Aachen. Commander: General der Panzertruppen Erich Brandenberger. Opponents: US First Army (VII and XIX Corps).
